items.title: Foreigners’ registration offices in all State Capitals by 2027: MHA
points: The Union government plans to establish Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) in all State capitals by 2027, the Ministry of Home Affairs said on Monday (November 2, 2026).
Since 2025, five new FRROs have been established, including two this year.

The decision follows directions from Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who has asked authorities to expand the FRRO network amid a rise in the number of foreigners arriving in India for tourism, medical treatment, and education.
Since 2025, FRROs have been opened in Jaipur, Chandigarh, and Guwahati, bringing regions previously administered by the Delhi, Amritsar and Kolkata FRROs under local jurisdiction.
This year, two more FRROs have become operational in Aizawl in Mizoram and Amravati in Andhra Pradesh.

The offices are located in Ahmedabad, Amravati, Amritsar, Aizawl, Agartala, Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar, Calicut, Chennai, Cochin, Chandigarh, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Kohima, Kozhikode, Lucknow, Mumbai, and Thiruvananthapuram.

items.title: 34-year-old man held for snatching elderly woman’s gold chain in Saidabad
points: A 34-year-old man was arrested for snatching a gold chain from an elderly woman in Saidabad, with police recovering the 17.160-gram chain and a motorcycle used in the offence, together worth about ₹3.50 lakh.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu: Collector takes stock of situation near Budameru rivulet as heavy inflows likely
points: Lakshmisha inspecting the situation in areas located near Budameru rivulet, on Monday. | Photo Credit: HANDOUT The NTR district administration has been put on full alert in view of the possibility of widespread heavy rainfall in Budameru catchment areas…
Lakshmisha on Monday conducted an extensive field inspection of Gudavalli and Enikepadu areas along the Budameru river and inspected the flow and the prevailing ground-level conditions.
He directed officials to ensure that there were no obstructions to the flow of floodwater, even if heavy inflows entered the catchment areas.
Water hyacinth and other waste materials near culverts and bridges should be removed regularly to facilitate the smooth flow of water, he said.
The Collector emphasised that irrigation, revenue and municipal officials must remain constantly alert at the field level.
He also instructed officials to keep sandbags ready near vulnerable and weakened embankments as a precautionary measure.

items.title: Surge in Reliance lifts Sensex by 1.6%; Nifty tops 23,400
points: A nearly 12 per cent surge in Reliance Industries, its third-biggest single-day gain in the past 10 years, powered Indian equities sharply higher on Monday.

The stock accounted for about 61 per cent of the Sensex’s gains and nearly half of the Nifty 50 rise, helping the benchmarks extend their winning streak to a third consecutive session amid falling crude oil prices, foreign fund inflows and improving risk…

items.title: One-time settlement scheme to clear motor vehicle tax arrears
points: Updated - November 02, 2026 09:30 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The State government has announced a ‘one-time settlement’ scheme to clear motor vehicle tax arrears in the State.
Vehicle owners with tax arrears spanning four years or more up to March 31, 2026, are eligible to benefit from the scheme.
The deadline to avail of this offer is March 31, 2027.
An official notification regarding this has been issued.
Under the scheme, owners of non-transport vehicles are required to pay 40% of their total tax arrears (including fines and interest) accumulated over the four years ending March 31, 2026.
For transport vehicles, the required payment is 30% of the total tax arrears (including fines and interest) for the same four-year period.

Those who opt for this scheme will be granted exemptions from the ‘Green Tax,’ fees related to the production of registration certificates, and contributions to the Motor Transport Workers’ Welfare Fund.

items.title: Patient dies at McGann Hospital entrance, waiting for stretcher; relatives allege negligence of staff
points: Relatives of a 60-year-old stroke patient have accused the staff of McGann Hospital, the teaching hospital in Shivamogga, of negligence after he died on Monday while waiting at the entrance for a stretcher.
Karibasappa of Muduvala, near Harnahalli in Shivamogga taluk, suffered a stroke a few days ago and was under treatment.
Early on Monday, he developed complications.
On the advice of a doctor at Harnahalli, the relatives took him to McGann Hospital in a private vehicle without waiting for an ambulance.
On reaching the hospital, the security staff stopped them and asked them to wait as a stretcher was not readily available.
The relatives said they insisted on carrying him in themselves, but the staff did not allow it.
Jagadish, a resident of Muduvala, said the patient was made to wait for nearly half an hour and was dead by then.
The relatives argued with the staff after the death and held them responsible.
